title: Level-order array omitting intermediate empty slots
summary: When empty slots inside a tree are omitted, the compacted level-order array shifts indices out of alignment, allowing the same value sequence to match different tree shapes.
context: In the table, "Original tree position" refers to the zero-based level-order position when empty slots are kept, with the root at position 0; "Compacted array index" refers to the array index after skipping empty slots. Only the original tree below is drawn in the figure.

The original tree has 10 nodes: root 1 (position 0) has left and right children 2 (position 1) and 3 (position 2); 2 has only left child 4 (position 3); 3 has left and right children 6 (position 5) and 7 (position 6); 4 has left and right children 8 (position 7) and 9 (position 8); 6 has only left child 12 (position 11); 7 has only right child 15 (position 14); and 8, 9, 12, and 15 are leaf nodes. The table below maps compacted array indices 0 through 9 to their original tree positions.
result: Once intermediate empty slots are omitted, the same level-order value sequence can correspond to differently connected trees. This issue arises only when empty slots occur in the middle; in a complete binary tree, all empty slots lie at the end of level order, so omitting trailing empty slots preserves the index mapping.

frames.title: Level-order array omitting intermediate empty slots
frames.explanation: The original tree is missing nodes at positions 4, 9, 10, 12, and 13; skipping empty slots to compact the sequence directly into [1, 2, 3, 4, 6, 7, 8, 9, 12, 15] shifts node 6 forward from original position 5 to compacted index 4. Applying 2i+2 then misidentifies 6 at index 4 as the right child of node 2 at index 1, whereas in the original tree 2 has no right child and 6 is the left child of 3. Deriving a whole tree from the compacted array via the index formulas yields: 1 with left 2 and right 3; 2 with left 4 and right 6; 3 with left 7 and right 8; 4 with left 9 and right 12; 6 with only left 15; and all remaining nodes as leaves. That derived tree has different connections from the original tree despite sharing the same level-order value sequence; it is an analytical comparison and is not drawn separately in the figure.
